decisions.rationale: BrowserQueryOptionsBase adds supportedDialogKinds?: string[]. This browser transport option does not apply: Local and cloud use the Node SDK query API, whose dialog options are already configured independently.

resumeSseStream(query): boolean is a new Browser SDK export. Neither the Local adapter nor the standalone cloud worker uses the Browser SDK or its SSE query transport; no resume integration is needed for this Node SDK update.

suspendSseStream(query): boolean is a new Browser SDK export. Local and cloud queries run through the Node SDK; browser SSE suspension is outside the integration and is not a substitute for Zeros turn cancellation.

core.d.ts re-exports BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES and LEGACY_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES from ./sdk.js. The desktop contract imports both runtime entry points and verifies that their inventories agree; desktop and standalone worker tests validate the names Zeros actually handles.

ArtifactOutput adds optional owned flags to five artifact/asset output variants. Zeros keeps the existing bounded tool-content/resource-link handling and does not map this provider flag to Zeros workspace ownership or new artifact UI.

CronCreateOutput adds nextFireAt?: number. The native next-fire timestamp is not yet consumed together with the lifecycle wake-up source; existing cron/tool handling makes no next-fire scheduling or idle-retention claim for this field.

CronListOutput.jobs entries add nextFireAt?: number. The native next-fire timestamp is not yet consumed together with the lifecycle wake-up source; existing cron/tool handling makes no next-fire scheduling or idle-retention claim for this field.

BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES supplies the runtime inventory for contract tests over the actual desktop adapters, renderer title matchers and standalone cloud worker. Every special-cased name must be canonical, an SDK legacy alias or an explicitly documented retired compatibility name. The existing edit-tool set and canonical Agent name also use the tuple type; inventory membership alone never enables a product feature.

LEGACY_TOOL_NAME_ALIASES supplies subagent aliases to both Node translators. Matching remains anchored and case-insensitive; native names, persisted identities and current output stay unchanged. Contract tests require each legacy spelling to have its canonical target covered by the same surface, and an injected SDK alias proves that routing follows the export. Mixed-provider renderer fallbacks retain their existing behavior under source assertions without importing the Node SDK into the renderer.

McpSdkServerConfig adds tools?: McpServerToolPolicy[] for host-registered SDK servers. Policy interpretation remains in the Node SDK/CLI. Zeros adds no per-tool policy override and preserves existing MCP configuration and approval behavior in both placements.

Query.reloadPlugins options add addPlugins?: SdkPluginConfig[]. Zeros lists and refreshes Claude plugins but has no flow that enables one, so the additive option has no caller. Existing no-argument reloads remain valid; adoption is deferred until Zeros can enable plugins.

SDKControlElicitationRequest.property_order is not applicable to host adoption: the SDK does not forward it to onElicitation. Its documented order already follows JavaScript object-key order, including index-like names first, which the existing requestedSchema.properties iteration preserves. Local forms and the cloud cancellation response need no change.

SDKControlGetContextUsageResponse adds category id, per-server mcpInstructions token shares, customAgents pluginId/path, and skills pluginName/pluginId/path metadata. Stable category IDs and per-server MCP shares are not yet mapped in the Local adapter or cloud worker. Optional plugin/path metadata is not presented.

SDKControlGetUsageResponse extends both behavior summaries with max_effort, workflow, always_on_context and large_tool_results, plus optional recommendations and fix objects. This usage API is experimental and remains unused; Zeros does not expose or depend on it in Local or cloud.

SDKControlInitializeRequest.sdkMcpServerConfigs entries add tools?: McpServerToolPolicy[]. The Node wrapper owns this control-handshake serialization. Zeros uses query() rather than authoring initialize frames and supplies no new SDK-server permission policy.

SDKControlMcpCallRequest adds result_not_for_model?: boolean, a capability-gated app-only result mode. Zeros does not issue these direct MCP control calls or enable this mode; existing agent tool results and their transcript handling are unchanged.

SDKControlMcpStatusRequest adds liveReply?: boolean for upstream CCR/Remote Control live event streams. Zeros Local and cloud run the Node SDK with stdio, not that upstream cloud transport; existing mcpServerStatus() calls keep the wrapper's normal response behavior.

SDKControlReloadPluginsRequest adds wire field add_plugins?: SdkPluginConfig[], corresponding to Query.reloadPlugins({ addPlugins }). Zeros has no flow that enables a plugin and therefore no caller for additive loading. Adoption is deferred until that flow exists; existing no-argument reloads keep their behavior.

SandboxSettingsSchema adds optional allowNestedUserNamespaces. The CLI defaults it to false and owns native settings validation. Zeros supplies no override for this setting; existing Local permissions and cloud VM isolation remain unchanged.

Settings adds attributionProject, attributionProjectPolicy.default, sshHostCommands and sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces. These remain native SDK/CLI settings; Zeros exposes none of these fields as a preference, telemetry mapping, SSH command surface or sandbox override, and retains each placement's existing settings sources.
